# Charter — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

- **Project:** S18 'Kata continuous improvement', track v1, ADM phase G, delivery plateau, tranche 9, plan `docs/plans/slices/S18-kata-improvement.md`. The project row `01a1d039-0d30-7f95-9d93-30eaabfec6da` is active at the pinned 2026-11-28 snapshot, its measured status is built against a plan status of planned, and its viability is rework.
- **Sponsor:** the programme's sponsoring group (`01a1d039-0d24-7d16-ae52-4841e96ccfac`), through the tranche-9 PI plan and the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`; the P0 project of record is `01a1dcb8-d24b-76de-b901-56fd56e001bc`.
- **Authority:** SPEC V2 §3 D24 with §5.7, §6 and the §8 S18 definition. The slice adds the `benchmark` module and the action `benchmark_runs.trend`, adds no table and no event, and its parity id is `PENDING-S0` because it ports no old surface.
- **Objective:** the benchmark becomes the kata loop's measuring instrument. A `conveyor`-arm run measures one pinned `capability_agent` or `procedure` version against the suite; two such runs are compared with S17's exact McNemar; one is promoted as the suite's baseline; and the improvement iteration — start a candidate, wait, compare, keep or revert — is a durable job that invokes exactly the actions a person would.
- **Scope:** the `conveyor` arm's producer, the version pinning on the run, `benchmark_runs.trend`, the improvement job `benchmark.improvement.run`, the baseline and regression semantics, and screen 14's data contract declared for S12. Out of scope are a new agent runtime or a second model loop, automatic code changes, any new table or event, and a second benchmark driver.
- **Acceptance:** the plan's §7 gate — the three named test targets `benchmark_arm`, `benchmark_trend` and `benchmark_improvement`, the OpenAPI `--check-lock`, the workspace suite and clippy — carried by the project's manifest `acceptance/programme/S18.toml`; the end-to-end proof is one real katas-tenant iteration.
- **Status:** the project stays active; this charter is authored retrospectively for the tranche-9 viability rework and does not claim the product's gate has been re-run for the pack. Issue #12 is open and carries the live kata proof; issue #30 is closed at the snapshot; tranche 9 `01a1e9e1-20dd-7cda-bd8b-e4fabe1d5db9` is not yet authorised.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

body.assignment: The architecture work assigns S18 the kata loop's measuring instrument: the benchmark stops being a harness read on its own and becomes the fixed point against which every improvement candidate is judged. The `conveyor` arm starts one conveyor run per benchmark instance through the same public action surface a person uses, waits for the terminal state, and takes the patch from the run's output; the run row pins `subject_kind` and the `capability_agent` or `procedure` id, so a measurement always names the version that produced it. The improvement job starts a candidate, waits on `benchmark_run.changed` or `get`, compares it with the promoted baseline and records `keep`, `revert` or `inconclusive` with the McNemar delta. The statement is retrospective: it describes the assignment the plan set and the state the 2026-11-28 snapshot carries.
body.scope: In scope are the `conveyor` arm producer, the version pinning on the run, `benchmark_runs.trend` behind `benchmarks:read`, the improvement job `benchmark.improvement.run`, the baseline and regression semantics, and screen 14's data contract declared for S12. Out of scope are a new agent runtime or a second model loop — the arm calls S13's `agent.run` exactly as a card run does — automatic code changes, any new table or event, and a second benchmark driver. The trend is a query over the stored `benchmark_run` and `benchmark_case` rows; nothing is rolled up into a table of its own.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors this retrospective set under the standing delegation; the Architecture Board reviews the Phase A–D artefacts and this statement; the SRO is accountable for the kata improvement capability and the tranche outcome; the kata coach or improvement procedure author chooses the candidate and reads the comparison; S15 owns `capability_agent` and the readiness check that refuses an unusable binding before a run; S17 owns the run, the compare, the promote, the arms and the reaper; and S12 owns screen 14, which S18 declares so it cannot be invented. The author of the pack is not the accepting role, so the programme's separation of duties holds.
body.acceptance_criteria: The gate is the plan's §7 sequence: `benchmark_arm` proves the arm refuses before S13/S15 data exists and runs when it does, exercising the three failure classes — `no_attempt`, `fail` and a typed refusal; `benchmark_trend` proves two versions of one subject compare with an exact McNemar delta; `benchmark_improvement` proves the improvement job performs the same calls a person does; `--print-openapi --check-lock` proves the served surface; the workspace suite and clippy close the gate. The end-to-end proof is one real katas-tenant iteration: a candidate `capability_agent` version, one run, a comparison against the promoted baseline and a recorded keep or revert, with the screen showing the same numbers. `acceptance/programme/S18.toml` is the manifest that carries this acceptance.
body.contract: The contract commits to one measurement path: every run is started, read and compared through the public action surface — `benchmark_runs.start`, `benchmark_runs.get` and `benchmark_runs.compare` — and the producer may not read `benchmark_instance`, may not write a case verdict, and may not run the instance in a tenant other than the one that owns the run. The trend is computed from stored rows and adds no table. The baseline is per suite and promoted explicitly by `promote`, never by a newer run arriving. A regression is McNemar p < 0.05 with a negative delta and both runs `control_ok=true`; the flag is recorded, and the revert stays a decision rather than an automatic act. S17's `benchmark.reap` owns the stale case, so a dead improvement job never holds a run.
body.retrospective: This statement is authored on 2026-11-28 for the tranche-9 viability rework. No contemporaneous statement of architecture work exists: the delivery was recorded in the slice plan and its issues, the project row stays active, issue #12 is open and issue #30 is closed at the snapshot. The statement therefore records the terms the plan sets, the four decisions §9 closes and the open questions §10 leaves, and it names what the snapshot does and does not prove rather than implying a ceremonial review that never happened.

# Solution Concept Diagram — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (Phase A)

## Metadata

Type diagram; phase A; plateau psa; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S18; tranche 9; retrospective under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`. This artefact is authored by the tranche-9 viability rework and does not attest contemporaneous intent.

## Entries

The concept has seven parts. The producer starts one conveyor run per instance through the public action and takes the patch from the run's output; the run row pins the subject; the trend is a query over stored runs and cases; the improvement job starts, waits, compares and records; the baseline is promoted and the regression rule reads McNemar with both controls; screen 14 presents the points and the flags; and S17's reaper owns the stale case. The entries deliberately show the seams the plan's traps defend.

## Links

Realizes the Requirements Catalog; depends on the Business Capability Map and the Data Entity catalog. The source is `docs/plans/slices/S18-kata-improvement.md` §5, whose deliverable list is the component map, and the module list `benchmark` with the read routes and the worker arm. The diagram is textual because the record's artefact action carries entries rather than an image.

The diagram keeps the measurement outside S18's own runtime: every run is a conveyor run through S13's `agent.run`, started by the same action a person uses, so the arm measures the product rather than a second implementation of it. It is published as an architecture-artifact-instance by the rework factory, and its whole point is that the trend, the baseline and the verdict are rows and calls, while the screen only displays them.

# Technology Standards Catalog — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (Phase D)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase D; plateau hld; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S18; tranche 9; retrospective under the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`. This artefact is authored by the tranche-9 viability rework and does not attest contemporaneous intent.

## Entries

Six standards, each with the failure it prevents. Postgres row-level security with a tenant column on every row keeps a producer from running an instance in a tenant other than the run's; the empty `adds_tables` keeps the trend derived rather than rolled up; the public action surface keeps the loop from becoming a second implementation; the exact McNemar through S17 keeps one statistical path; the OpenAPI lock keeps the served surface equal to the checked-in document; and the GitHub-hosted preflight is the compile verdict under the 2026-11-20 owner direction.

## Links

Derives from the Data Entity catalog; realizes the technology half of the Solution Concept Diagram; reuses the platform's existing RLS, migration, action, job and lock conventions rather than adding a parallel one. The source is the plan's §3, §7 and §8, which record each rule against a measured failure mode — the non-comparable run, the second executor, the drifting roll-up — rather than a preference.

## Document

The catalog is published as an architecture-artifact-instance by the rework factory. The standards are the ones the plan actually leans on: a reader can see which failure each convention prevents, which is what makes them enforceable in review instead of aspirational. No migration is S18's default, and any migration that is added would be proven through the sqlx ledger rather than a log line.

# Architecture Artefact Index — S18 (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Metadata

The artefact set for S18 is the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts on the delivery track: the Stakeholder Map, the Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog, the Requirements Catalog and the Solution Concept Diagram at phase a, plateau psa; the Business Capability Map at phase b; the Data Entity/Data Component Catalog at phase c; and the Technology Standards Catalog at phase d, the last three at plateau hld. Each carries an authored body dated 2026-11-28; the owner is the programme architect under the tranche-9 rework delegation, the reviewer is the Architecture Board, and the subject is this project's record at the pinned snapshot.

## Entries

Seven rows in the order the standard seeds them: a/matrix — Stakeholder Map — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (Phase A); a/catalog — Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (Phase A); a/catalog — Requirements Catalog — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (Phase A); a/diagram — Solution Concept Diagram — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (Phase A); b/diagram — Business Capability Map — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (Phase B); c/catalog — Data Entity/Data Component Catalog — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (Phase C); d/catalog — Technology Standards Catalog — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (Phase D).

## Links

Every artefact links to another artefact of the set with one of the four kinds the record's link action allows: derivation, realization, reuse or dependency. The links follow the phase order, so a reader can walk from A to D without an orphan, and each artefact's own Links section names its source in the slice plan and the tree. The deepest source is `docs/plans/slices/S18-kata-improvement.md` §3, §5, §7, §8 and §9.

## Document

This index is published as its own architecture-artifact document by the rework factory. It is the document the close gate reads for the project's artefact standard, and it is why the set can be verified without re-reading the plan: the titles, the order and the link kinds are all stated here, and the seven rows match the seven artefacts one for one. # Inception Analysis — S18 Kata continuous improvement (retrospective, Phase G)

## Current state

The project row is active, measured built, at ADM phase G on the delivery plateau in tranche 9, while the slice plan still records its status as planned — a mismatch the tranche-9 viability rework exists to reconcile, not to hide. The tree holds the three product suites and the web contract, but the snapshot carried no charter, baseline, registers, contract or Phase-G review, which is why the measured inventory is 4 open packages, 3 P1 and 1 P2 (`wbs_absent`).

## Reuse sources

S17 supplies benchmark_run and benchmark_case, the driver, compare, promote, the arms and the reaper; S13 supplies agent.run with the resolved capability_agent in the step input; S15 supplies capability_agent and the readiness check that refuses an unusable binding before a run. The plan's source table also points at the internal step-invocation path and the executor slot's rules, and the producer reuses the public action surface rather than a private path.

## Build vs reuse

Build the conveyor arm's producer, benchmark_runs.trend, benchmark.improvement.run and screen 14's declared data contract; reuse S17's stored rows and its start, get, compare and promote, S13's agent.run and S15's readiness check. The plan refuses a new agent runtime or second model loop, automatic code changes, any new table or event and a second benchmark driver, so the trend stays a query over the stored rows and the job stays one queue row.

## Risks

Four risks are carried in the pack's risk register: a non-comparable run averaged into the trend; the improvement job becoming a second state machine that holds a run; a one- or two-instance win read as signal when identical baselines differ by four; and a run with no pinned subject. Each has an owning requirement and existing coverage — crates/api/tests/benchmark_arm.rs and crates/api/tests/benchmark_trend.rs among the suites — and none is discharged by prose alone.

# Architecture Analysis — S18 Kata continuous improvement (retrospective, Phase G)

## Current state

At the 2026-11-28 snapshot the benchmark is already one instrument on the conveyor's public surface: S17 stores benchmark_run and benchmark_case and offers start, get, compare and promote, while S18 adds the conveyor arm's producer, benchmark_runs.trend behind benchmarks:read and the durable job benchmark.improvement.run. The project row is active and measured built in tranche 9; the lifecycle record is what the 3 P1 packages and `wbs_absent` say is missing.

## Options considered

Three options were weighed. A second benchmark driver or a private executor was refused because it would measure a second implementation of the conveyor rather than the product. A roll-up table for the trend was refused because it would drift from the raw rows; the trend is a query. A job with its own state machine was refused because S17's benchmark.reap owns staleness and the run keeps its own lifecycle. The chosen design keeps one action surface, one statistical path and one promoted baseline per suite.

## Risks

The comparison is only as good as its pairing: the same 50 instances, suite hashes, grader and prompt/oracle pair, with a non-comparable run refused rather than averaged. The plan records that two byte-identical baselines can differ by four instances, so a small delta is not evidence. A run without a pinned subject measures nothing, and a wedged job must not hold a run; crates/api/tests/benchmark_trend.rs and apps/server/tests/benchmark_improvement.rs exercise the trend and the job.

## Dependency map

S13 supplies agent.run, the bounded internal loop that takes the resolved capability_agent in the step input; S15 supplies capability, capability_agent and the readiness check that refuses an unusable binding before a run; S17 supplies the run and case rows, the driver, compare, promote, the arms and the reaper. None is optional: without S17 there is no measurement, and without S13 and S15 the arm has nothing to invoke. The linked issue #12 is open and carries the live kata proof.

# Architecture Design — S18 Kata continuous improvement (retrospective, Phase G)

## Context and boundary

The design keeps the measurement outside S18's runtime: every benchmark run is a conveyor run started through the action a person uses, with the patch taken from the run's output. In scope are the producer, the subject pinning, benchmark_runs.trend, benchmark.improvement.run, the baseline and regression semantics, and screen 14's declared data contract. Out of scope are a model loop, a private executor, a new table or event, and a second benchmark driver.

## Aggregates, tables and actions

S17's benchmark_run and benchmark_case remain the aggregate; a run pins subject_kind and the capability_agent or procedure id, and S17's CHECK refuses a suite subject with arm conveyor. S18 adds no table. The two new actions are benchmark_runs.trend and benchmark.improvement.run, reusing benchmark_runs.start, benchmark_runs.get, benchmark_runs.compare and benchmark_runs.promote; the job records keep, revert or inconclusive with the McNemar delta on an existing queue row.

## Decisions

The plan's §9 closes four decisions: the improvement loop is a consumer of the action registry with no private store or privileged path; the baseline is per suite and promoted explicitly, never because a newer run arrived; the trend is a query, not a table; and a trend point is only a run of the same suite and arm. A regression is McNemar p < 0.05 with a negative delta and both runs control_ok=true; the flag is recorded and the revert stays a decision.

## Acceptance

The plan's §7 gate names three targets: cargo test -p conveyor-api --test benchmark_arm, cargo test -p conveyor-api --test benchmark_trend and cargo test -p conveyor-server --test benchmark_improvement, plus the --print-openapi --check-lock command, the workspace suite and clippy. Re-measured 2026-11-28, the suites sit at crates/api/tests/benchmark_arm.rs, crates/api/tests/benchmark_trend.rs and apps/server/tests/benchmark_improvement.rs, and the web contract at apps/web/e2e/improvement.spec.ts.

## Architecture artefacts

The seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts are the pack's architecture-artifact rows: the Stakeholder Map, the Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog, the Requirements Catalog and the Solution Concept Diagram at phase A; the Business Capability Map at phase B; the Data Entity/Data Component Catalog at phase C; and the Technology Standards Catalog at phase D. # Statement of Architecture Work — S18 Kata continuous improvement (retrospective, Phase G)

## Assignment

Assign S18 the kata loop's measuring instrument: the conveyor arm starts one conveyor run per benchmark instance through the public action surface, waits for the terminal state and takes the patch from the run's output; the run pins subject_kind and its version id; two runs are compared with S17's exact McNemar; and the improvement job records keep, revert or inconclusive with the delta. The statement is retrospective — it records the assignment the plan set and the state the 2026-11-28 snapshot carries.

## Scope

In scope are the conveyor arm producer, the version pinning, benchmark_runs.trend behind benchmarks:read, benchmark.improvement.run, the baseline and regression semantics, and screen 14's declared data contract. Out of scope are a new agent runtime or second model loop, automatic code changes, any new table or event, and a second benchmark driver. The trend is computed from stored benchmark_run and benchmark_case rows; nothing is rolled up into a table.

## Responsibilities

The programme architect authors the retrospective set; the Architecture Board reviews the Phase A–D artefacts and this statement; the SRO is accountable for the kata improvement capability and the tranche outcome; the kata coach or improvement procedure author chooses the candidate and reads the comparison. S15 owns capability_agent and readiness, S17 owns the run, compare, promote, arms and reaper, and S12 owns screen 14. The pack's author is not the accepting role.

## Acceptance criteria

The gate is the plan's §7 sequence: cargo test -p conveyor-api --test benchmark_arm proves the arm refuses before S13/S15 data exists and runs when it does; cargo test -p conveyor-api --test benchmark_trend proves two versions of one subject compare with an exact McNemar delta; cargo test -p conveyor-server --test benchmark_improvement proves the job performs the same calls a person does; the OpenAPI lock, the workspace suite and clippy close it. The end-to-end proof is one real katas-tenant iteration on issue #12.

## Contract

The contract commits to one measurement path: every run is started, read and compared through benchmark_runs.start, benchmark_runs.get and benchmark_runs.compare, and the producer may not read benchmark_instance, write a case verdict, or run an instance in a tenant other than the run's. It commits to the trend as a query, an explicit promote per suite, and a regression flag that records rather than reverts. S17's benchmark.reap owns the stale case, so a dead job never holds a run.

# User stories — S18 Kata continuous improvement (retrospective, Phase G)

## Personas

A kata coach who runs the improvement loop and decides whether a candidate is kept or reverted; a capability owner who publishes a capability_agent version and needs to see it measured; and a reviewer who must be able to read the same comparison the job invoked. Each is a role the slice plan names, and none is a screen user of S18's own making: screen 14 is declared for S12.

## Stories

As a kata coach, I want a benchmark run to pin the subject version that produced it, so that a keep or revert decision names what was measured. As a capability owner, I want my candidate compared with the promoted baseline on paired instances, so that a one-instance win is not read as an improvement. As a reviewer, I want the trend and the verdict derived from the same stored rows, so that I can recompute the decision the job recorded.

## Scenarios

S1 a missing or unready binding is 409 arm_not_ready before the first case; S2 a scope, prompt or capability failure is recorded as no_attempt, never as a model failure; S3 two versions of one subject compare with an exact McNemar delta and direction; S4 a non-comparable run is refused and surfaced, not averaged; S5 the job starts, waits, compares and records keep, revert or inconclusive; S6 a dead job leaves the run's lifecycle to S17's benchmark.reap.

## Verify

cargo test -p conveyor-api --test benchmark_arm, cargo test -p conveyor-api --test benchmark_trend and cargo test -p conveyor-server --test benchmark_improvement are the plan's §7 targets, and all three suites exist in the tree on 2026-11-28; the web contract is npx playwright test apps/web/e2e/improvement.spec.ts, whose spec also exists. The pack's own content check and receipt verify the record, not the product gate.

risk.title: A run that is not comparable is averaged into the trend and reads as signal
risk.body: The plan's trap 3 records that S17's compare refuses a comparison across a different oracle or prompt, and the trend must surface that refusal rather than average over it. If the trend joined points across a changed grader, prompt or oracle, a rate difference would look like a candidate win while in fact measuring a different instrument. The response is to display the run with its refusal and control state and never plot it against the capability baseline.
risk.response: Surface the compare refusal on the point, key the baseline line to suite and arm only, and treat any comparability mismatch as an inconclusive verdict rather than a delta.

risk.title: The improvement job becomes a second state machine and holds a run
risk.body: The plan's trap 5 records that a dead improvement job must not hold a run: the run keeps its own lifecycle, the job is replaceable, and S17's benchmark.reap owns the stale case. A job that tracked its own progress outside the run would duplicate the state machine, and a wedged job row would make a healthy run look stuck. The response is to keep the job a queue row whose only outputs are the recorded verdict and the calls it made.
risk.response: Reap through benchmark.reap, keep the verdict on the job row, and prove in benchmark_improvement that a dead job leaves the run's lifecycle untouched.

risk.title: A small win is noise: two byte-identical baseline runs differ by four instances
risk.body: The plan's §1 records the old harness's measurement that two byte-identical baseline runs can differ by four instances, so a candidate that wins by one or two has not won anything. The exact test must decide whether the discordant pairs exceed noise, and the regression rule requires both runs control_ok=true. Without that discipline a rate delta would be read as an improvement, which is exactly the failure the benchmark is being pulled into the conveyor to prevent.
risk.response: Record the keep, revert or inconclusive verdict with the McNemar delta, demand p < 0.05 with a negative delta for a regression, and refuse to plot a point whose controls failed.

risk.title: A run without a pinned subject version measures nothing comparable
risk.body: The plan's trap 2 records that version pinning is the measurement: a run without capability_agent_id or procedure_id cannot say which version produced it, and a suite subject with arm conveyor is refused by S17's CHECK. A trend that plotted a run with no pinned subject would mix versions under one line. The response is to treat the pin as a precondition of comparability and let the run row carry the id the verdict is read against.
risk.response: Refuse to start a measurement without a pinned subject, keep the suite and arm restriction on the trend, and assert the pin in benchmark_arm.

The project row, its dependency edges and its measured status are read there; a row that changes when the build lane merges is out of scope until the pack is re-preflighted, which is why the pack quotes the snapshot rather than the live service.

assumption.title: A comparison is genuinely paired: same instances, suite hashes, grader and prompt/oracle pair

The assumption is that S17's compare enforces those equalities and that the trend can surface the refusal; the benefit of the exact test depends on the pair actually being paired.

dependency.title: S18 depends on S13, S15 and S17
dependency.body: The plan's frontmatter declares depends_on: [S13, S15, S17], and the project row records the same three needs. S13 supplies agent.run, the bounded internal loop that takes its resolved capability_agent in the step input; S15 supplies capability, capability_agent and the readiness check; and S17 supplies the run and case rows, the driver, compare, promote, the arms and the reaper. None of the three is optional: without S17 there is no measurement, and without S13 and S15 the arm has nothing to invoke.

dependency.title: S18 unblocks the kata procedure's use of the trend and S12's screen 14
dependency.body: The improvement job and the trend are the surface the kata's own procedure reads when it chooses the next candidate, and screen 14 is declared for S12 so that the screen cannot invent its own contract. The dependency runs from S18 to both consumers: the actions, scopes and SSE topics must exist before the screen can bind, and the procedure cannot read a trend that does not answer. No UI is built inside S18.

dependency.title: Issue #12 carries the live kata proof and is open at the snapshot
dependency.body: The plan's §7 names the end-to-end proof as one real katas-tenant iteration: a candidate capability_agent version, one run, a comparison against the promoted baseline and a recorded keep or revert, with the screen showing the same numbers. benefit.title: A candidate is accepted or refused on an exact paired test, not on a raw rate delta
benefit.body: The verdict carries the McNemar delta — the discordant pairs, the p-value and the direction — and the regression rule demands p < 0.05 with a negative delta and both runs control_ok=true. The benefit is that a one or two instance difference, which two byte-identical baselines can produce by themselves, cannot be read as an improvement, and a reviewer can recompute the decision from the same comparison the job invoked.

benefit.title: The instrument and the loop cannot drift apart: one action surface, one statistic, one baseline
benefit.body: The producer, the improvement job and a person all start, read and compare runs through the same actions; the trend is computed from the same stored rows the comparison reads; and the baseline is the run promote recorded. The benefit is that there is no second implementation of the conveyor to measure and no roll-up to disagree with the raw data, so a trend cannot silently become a different instrument from the one that judged the candidate.

benefit.title: A regression is flagged with its controls, and the revert stays a recorded decision
benefit.body: A regression flag is McNemar p < 0.05 with a negative delta and both runs control_ok=true, and the job records keep, revert or inconclusive rather than mutating the run or the baseline. The benefit is that a person can always read the same comparison the job read, and the kata's own procedure decides whether to revert — the flag informs the decision without taking it, which is the difference between an instrument and an automation.

# Project Brief — S18 Kata Continuous Improvement (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Outcome

The benchmark becomes the kata loop's measuring instrument, so the question 'did this candidate version help?' gets an answer before it gets a process: a `conveyor`-arm run measures one pinned `capability_agent` or `procedure` version on the same 50 instances with the same suite hashes, grader and prompt/oracle pair; two runs are compared with S17's exact McNemar; the promoted baseline is the fixed point every later run is read against; and the improvement iteration records keep, revert or inconclusive with the delta. Screen 14 shows the version-to-version trend and flags a significant regression with its controls.

## Boundary

It does not own a new agent runtime or a second model loop — the arm calls S13's `agent.run` exactly as a card run does — automatic code changes, any new table or event, or a second benchmark driver. Six build-order steps. Second `benchmark_runs.trend`, the query and its read model with the regression rule. Third the improvement job: enqueue, wait, compare, record, reaping through S17's `benchmark.reap`. ## Capabilities

Five. Measure a subject version: a pinned `capability_agent` or `procedure` version becomes a suite run. Compare against the baseline: two runs become an exact McNemar delta with its direction. Promote the baseline: one run becomes the suite's fixed point by an explicit act. Run the improvement iteration: a candidate becomes a recorded keep, revert or inconclusive.
